newsitem.title: USA: Cool air, no frost for Brazil coffee--Smith Barney.
newsitem.headline: Cool air, no frost for Brazil coffee--Smith Barney.

text.p: Brazilian coffee-growing areas are likely to see cooler weather this weekend, but temperatures will not be cold enough to cause any damage, Smith Barney meterologist Jon Davis said in his daily update on Monday.

A ridge of high pressure which has been positioned across the region during the past few weeks will weaken over the weekend and early next week, allowing some cooler air to make its way into the Brazil coffee belt, Davis said.
Lows on Sunday and Monday mornings are forecast to fall into the upper 40s to middle 50s F (8 to 12 C).
"This is quite a bit colder than temps have been lately, but still a long distance away from levels which would be a frost/freeze damage concern," Davis said in the report.

"Warmer weather is on tap during the early to middle portion of next week," he added. "Thus, during the next 10 days, there is only one time frame to monitor -- Sunday morning and Monday morning -- and this does not look like a threat."
Davis' forecast, however, differs from a weather outlook put out on Monday by Brazilian meterologists Somar.
Somar said a polar air mass, which may pass through Brazil's coffee regions from the evening of July 5, could represent the greatest threat of frost seen so far this year.

The air mass, currently expected to have an intensity of 1,032 millibars on July 4, could lead to temperatures of around zero degrees Celsius (32 F) in north Parana and southwest Sao Paulo states on the nights of July 5 and 6, Somar said.
